extraFacts.fact: NPT is the US tapered pipe thread standard, ASME B1.20.1; an ASME Class 150 (ASA 150) flange is the ASME B16.5 Class 150 bolt pattern.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1 (Pipe Threads, General Purpose, Inch); ASME B16.5 (Pipe Flanges and Flanged Fittings)

faqs.q: What is a zinc plated steel female flanged Bauer coupling used for?
faqs.a: A zinc-plated steel female flanged Bauer coupling is the Bauer female half with a bolted ASA (ASME) Class 150 flange back, for connecting a Bauer line to a Class 150 flanged pipe, pump or valve. Bauer-type couplings are lever-locked quick couplings for water, irrigation and slurry lines, and the tip seats like a ball in a cup, so the joint tolerates some misalignment.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the zinc plated steel female flanged Bauer coupling come in?
faqs.a: It is listed in 2", 3", 4", 6" and 8", five sizes in all, with Indus part numbers IH-BC-FLANGE-FEMALE-200 to IH-BC-FLANGE-FEMALE-800. Zinc-plated carbon steel is the body material, and the other materials in the family share the interface but can differ in length.

faqs.q: How do I read the maker part number BTC200FLF for a female flanged Bauer coupling?
faqs.a: In BTC200FLF, BTC is the maker's Bauer-type coupling code, 200 is the 2" size (300 is 3", 400 is 4") and FLF marks this style, so BTC300FLF is the 3" size. Indus part numbers such as IH-BC-FLANGE-FEMALE-200 carry the same size digits.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of the female flanged Bauer coupling?
faqs.a: The maker's datasheet gives up to 150 psi for the flanged Bauer couplings, so the working pressure is up to 150 psi. The listing does not state a temperature or a media limit; give us the medium and the pressure and we check it with the maker.

faqs.q: What is the female flanged Bauer coupling made of and what seals it?
faqs.a: The body of the female flanged Bauer coupling is zinc-plated carbon steel in 2", 3", 4", 6" and 8", and the seal is a rubber O-ring in the female half, as on the maker's drawing. Zinc plating protects the steel in water service; check the medium if it is aggressive or abrasive.

faqs.q: What does the female flanged Bauer coupling connect to?
faqs.a: It connects to a Bauer male half, such as the [male flanged half](/p/zinc-plated-steel-male-flanged-bauer-type-couplings) or a male hose shank half. The flange is ASA (ASME) Class 150, so the mating flange needs the same class and bolt circle. Keep Bauer and ring-lock halves apart, because the two patterns look alike; see [Bauer couplings explained](/blog/bauer-couplings-explained) for the differences.

faqs.q: Female flanged or male flanged Bauer coupling: which half do I need?
faqs.a: The female flanged half carries the O-ring and the lever ring, so it goes on the side that receives the male tip; the [male flanged half](/p/zinc-plated-steel-male-flanged-bauer-type-couplings) has the rounded tip. Choose by which side of the joint the flange sits on, and tell us the Class 150 flange you are bolting to.

faqs.q: What are the dimensions of the female flanged Bauer coupling in 2" and 8"?
faqs.a: The size table gives D 84 mm and L 145 mm in the 2" size and D 266 mm and L 270 mm in the 8" size. These are the maker's zinc-plated steel dimensions, converted to millimetres; other materials can differ, so ask for the drawing.
